title: An AI agent pays a UK shop straight from a bank account for the first time: nine mini pizzas
summary: In the FCA's sandbox, Papa John's AI agent took an order and paid from the customer's linked bank account through TrueLayer, under a spending limit set with Lloyds or NatWest. TrueLayer says it is a UK first; the Guardian reports it was nine mini margheritas.

topics.angle: Letting an AI agent spend your money, and what stops it spending too much.

claims.text: Papa John's and TrueLayer say they completed the UK's first agentic Pay by Bank payment, with an AI agent paying straight from the customer's linked bank account.
The customer sets a spending limit with their bank which cannot be exceeded by any AI agent, authorisation happens in the bank app, and no credentials are shared with the agent.
It was conducted through the FCA's Supercharged Sandbox and used Lloyds' and NatWest's variable recurring payment APIs.
The order was nine mini margherita pizzas, the Guardian reports.
TrueLayer's chief executive Francesco Simoneschi said 'This is possibly the last Black Friday as we know it', and that it still requires control and supervision.
claims.who: Francesco Simoneschi, TrueLayer, to BBC Radio 4 via The Guardian

claims.text: Earlier this week the FCA warned firms developing AI agents that they must comply with existing regulations.
Open banking lets banks share data or start payments with authorised third parties through APIs, which brings security risks such as phishing and over-broad access.
How the agent behaves outside a sandbox, with real customers at scale, is not tested yet.

to_find: The FCA's own account of the sandbox showcase on 26 November
would_change: A bank or the FCA reporting an agent payment that went past its limit.
